title: Southern Fried Chicken
subtitle: crispy spiced fried chicken
excerpt: Chicken thighs soaked in spiced milk, then dredged in seasoned flour and fried until golden. The buttermilk soak keeps the meat juicy while the coating crisps up. A true American classic.
sourceNotes: Southern fried chicken is a cornerstone of American Southern cooking, with roots in Scottish frying techniques and West African seasoning traditions brought together in the antebellum South.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Soak the chicken in spiced milk overnight in the fridge for deeper flavour.

content.text: Soaking the chicken in seasoned milk before coating it makes a huge difference to the final texture. Give it at least an hour, or overnight if you can. Keep the oil at a steady temperature -- too low and the coating absorbs grease, too high and the outside burns before the meat is cooked.
Mix the milk with 1 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp cayenne in a large bowl. Add the chicken pieces. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Mix the flour, baking powder, paprika, garlic powder, black pepper, and remaining salt in a shallow dish.
Lift the chicken from the milk, letting excess drip off. Dredge each piece in the flour mixture, pressing firmly so it coats all over.
Heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. The oil is ready when a pinch of flour sizzles immediately.
Fry the chicken in batches. Do not crowd the pan. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on a wire rack or kitchen paper. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.cause: Coating not pressed on firmly or oil not hot enough
items.fix: Press the flour onto the chicken firmly before frying. Make sure the oil is properly hot before adding the chicken.

items.symptom: Chicken is golden outside but raw inside
items.cause: Oil too hot, cooking too fast
items.fix: Reduce heat to medium after the first 2 minutes. Thighs need longer than you might expect -- check with a thermometer (75C) if unsure.
Wait until the oil reaches frying temperature before adding chicken. A kitchen thermometer is helpful here.

content.text: Southern fried chicken has deep roots in the American South. Scottish immigrants brought the tradition of frying chicken in fat. West African cooks added bold seasoning and refined the technique in plantation kitchens. Over time it became one of the most recognisable foods in American culture. Today it appears everywhere from roadside stalls to fine-dining menus.
